prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1127; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A dated inspection photo shows the same dent before this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported being struck from behind while stopped at a traffic signal. The claimant, a passenger in the insured vehicle, reported right shoulder pain at the scene and has since retained counsel, who asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: The responding officer's report records a rear impact and notes the claimant seated in the rear of the insured vehicle. Two independent witnesses at the intersection gave statements that match the accounts of the insured and the other driver.

Entry 3: Scene photographs show damage to the rear bumper and tailgate of the insured vehicle, and the damage to the front of the other vehicle lines up with it. The pattern and location fit the impact as reported.

Entry 4: Coverage review complete. The driver is listed on the policy, the policy was in force at the time of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 5: Claimant's counsel sent a medical summary describing a shoulder injury. The adjuster noted that the type of injury is what would be expected from a rear impact of this force. The claimant's account given by phone matched what was said at the scene.

Entry 6: Prior records were requested from the claimant's providers and the insurer's database. No earlier treatment or complaints involving the same shoulder are on file.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a usual course, beginning with physiotherapy and anti-inflammatory medication. The treating notes show steady improvement, with the number of sessions tapering as range of motion recovered.

Entry 8: An inspection photograph from an earlier vehicle inspection shows a dent in the same rear panel area that appears to match the damage now claimed. This conflicts with the other evidence and needs to be reconciled before the file moves forward. The adjuster has asked the insured and the repair facility for an explanation.

Entry 9: Claimant interviewed again with counsel present. The account was the same as in every prior conversation. The earlier photograph was raised, and counsel said they would respond after speaking with the client.

Entry 10: File referred for review of the prior-dent question. Reserve maintained pending counsel's response, and the next follow-up is set for the coming week.
